turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What brings you in here today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah hi, I'm I I have a pain in my belly. It started a couple hours ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and where exactly in your belly do you have this pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's mostly up here on the right side.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: The right side, OK and can you describe what kind of pain is it? Is it like a dull pain or sharp pain, an aching pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh I guess it's a, it's an aching pain I'd say. It kind of just, um, it would initially just come and go, but now it's just it's staying. It's not going away.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and so it's in the right area and does it travel anywhere elsewhere besides on from the right side?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And on a scale of 1 to 10, one being the least amount of pain you felt in your life, and 10 being the worst, how much would you rate it right now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's about to a 10, an 8 maybe.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: An 8, OK and so just to clarify, when did it start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: About 8 hours ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: 8 hours ago, OK. And were you doing anything before? Like, did you have a meal or how were you sleeping before it woke you up, what was going on before you had the pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I was just about to go to sleep. I wasn't doing anything in particular at the time.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And has it been getting worse since it first started?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh yeah, definitely it would come and go, but now for the past I'd say five to six hours, it's been constant, just there all the time.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you had any similar pain like this in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, uh I I have the same pain that sort of comes and goes after I eat. Usually after I've had something like a something fatty, something from outdoors, maybe like a burger or fries or something. I initially thought it was indigestion, but I don't I don't know what's going on now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and does it, does anything make it better or worse or anything that you've tried?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Well, I guess eating sometimes makes it worse, um, but I don't I don't think there's anything that's making it better.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you tried any medications at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I tried Tylenol but that didn't do anything.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And besides, uh, the pain that you're having, do you have any nausea and vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I am a little nauseous, but no, I didn't, haven't had I haven't vomited yet, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you been having any fevers?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I don't think so. I haven't checked. I don't feel feverish.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any sweats or like chills?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No,  I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any changes in your bowel movements like constipation, diarrhea?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Have you traveled anywhere recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you been feeling at all, very tired, not your usual self, fatigued?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Well the pain is making it difficult for me to do things, um, but I I guess I'm not, uh a little fatigued  maybe.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Um, have you been having any changes in your urinary patterns?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No? Any changes in your skin and you rashes, any yellowing of your skin?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nothing that I've noticed, no, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Any changes in your urine color?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you noticed blood in your stools at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I have not, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how about your appetite, has this changed at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Well, I guess because it's this thing happens usually happens after I eat, I think I've been eating less than usual, just because I don't, I don't want to, you know, I don't like the pain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any significant weight loss recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any recent infections recently at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, and otherwise are you, do you have any other medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure or anything else?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do have diabetes but that's about it I think.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And you take anything for your diabetes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I take metformin.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um do you take any other medications at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't, sorry, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No worries. Do you have any allergies to any medications, any environmental allergies?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No no, no, I don't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you been hospitalized in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no I haven't ever. I've been very uh healthy. No hospitalizations.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any past surgeries?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I got my wisdom teeth removed when I was a teenager.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Have you been in contact with anyone who has been ill recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Hmm, and in terms of your family history, has anyone had any cancers or um any err um IBD like Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that I know of.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And anything that runs in the family at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: My dad had a heart attack when he was in his 60s. But that's it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And um, currently right now do you work?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh no, I'm I'm laid off because of COVID.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And currently, what is your home situation like?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: What do you mean?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So do you live in an apartment, house and do you live with anyone?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I I I live in an apartment, I live alone.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, and in terms of your daily routine, do you feel that you get enough exercise? Do you go outside for walks or runs or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I usually go out for a run, especially when it's a little bit warmer, which it now is.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And do you do you drink alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, sometimes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How much would you say you drink in an average week?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: One to two drinks a day.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and what do you usually drink?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'll just drink a glass of wine at night, just helps me relax.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And do you smoke cigarettes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I don't, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And do you use any recreational drugs like marijuana?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright, so um, that's all the questions I have and just to clarify, does your pain come and go, or is it constant?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, so initially it would come and go, but now, so for the first 2 hours it would come and go. And when I would have this pain when I was eating, it would come and go. But over the past six hours it's just been constant.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright.
